items.title: Haywood Hillyer Interview, 1958-05-04
items.q: Except Myra Loppa... Who is this? And that's Myra Loppa, Mrs. Mendel... I knew her mother and father and all those people.

ctx.x: Do you remember when people... Did any of your contemporaries, your friends in New Orleans...

I can't remember... I can't remember... Can't remember any of them that I knew. Well... Cared for it. Except Myra Loppa, who we were little... I was slightly shocked when she took it up so seriously. Who is this? And that's Myra Loppa, Mrs. Mendel. Oh, that was years ago. That's what I wanted. I mean, that's years after a lifetime. She was younger than I. Well, it was the first time I remembered anybody in our... Crowd or set of people who took jazz seriously. Who? It was not in your set, did you? Not in our set.…
Well, do you remember when they started being played at David John's parties or at Falls or anything like that? No.
